title: Heparin Versus Saline Locking of Peripheral Venous Catheters
official: Heparin Versus Saline Locking of Peripheral Venous Catheters: a Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether locking peripheral venous catheters with heparin keeps them open (patent) better than locking them with saline, in adults admitted to hospital who have a peripheral venous catheter for intermittent treatment. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the percentage of blocked peripheral venous catheters higher in patients whose catheters are locked with saline than in those whose catheters are locked with heparin?
* Do the rates of other catheter-related complications (phlebitis, catheter-related bloodstream infection, extravasation, and leakage at the insertion site) differ between the two groups?
* Which clinical and drug-related factors are associated with catheter blockage?

Researchers will compare patients admitted to a hospital that routinely locks catheters with saline with patients admitted to a hospital that routinely locks catheters with heparin.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Admitted to Hospital Residència Sant Camil (CSAPG) or Hospital Comarcal de l'Alt Penedès (CSAPG) during the study period
* At least one peripheral venous catheter for intermittent treatment, not inserted in a medical emergency
* Aged 18 years or older

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known allergy to heparin
* Treatment with systemic unfractionated sodium heparin
* Dialysis
* Venous catheter used only for diagnostic tests
* Venous catheter used only for transfusion of blood products
* Participation in another clinical study with drugs or procedures that may affect catheter patency
* Severe heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in recent months
* Uncontrolled active bleeding during admission
* Cerebral aneurysm or dissecting aortic aneurysm, except in association with corrective surgery
* Confirmed or suspected cerebrovascular hemorrhage
* Severe uncontrolled hypertension
* Severe coagulation disorders: platelets below 30,000/µL, prothrombin time ratio above 1.7, or activated partial thromboplastin time ratio above 1.7
